items.explanation: Transparency mandates that data subjects are informed of processing details in an accessible and easily understood manner.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate Purpose dictates that processing must have a declared, specified, and lawful objective compatible with legal standards.
items.question_text: Which principle requires personal data to be processed solely for specific, declared purposes and not used for incompatible goals?
options: Proportionality
Legitimate Purpose
Confidentiality
Data Portability
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: The principle of Legitimate Purpose requires that all processing be tied to a declared, specific, and lawful purpose.

items.lesson_concept: Proportionality ensures that data processing is adequate, relevant, suitable, necessary, and not excessive relative to the stated purpose.
items.question_text: Collecting full genetic markers from a customer subscribing to a monthly magazine subscription violates which principle?
options: Legitimate Purpose
Transparency
Proportionality
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Proportionality
items.explanation: Requiring genetic data for a simple magazine subscription is excessive and unnecessary, violating Proportionality.

items.lesson_concept: Data collected for one specific purpose cannot be repurposed for direct marketing without a separate valid lawful basis or new consent.
items.question_text: A hotel collects guest passport numbers strictly for government security compliance, then re-uses the list to send promotional spa discounts without consent. What principle is breached?
options: Legitimate Purpose
Data Availability
Accuracy
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: Using mandatory security registration data for promotional marketing without authorization violates Legitimate Purpose.

items.lesson_concept: The principle of Accuracy requires PICs to maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date personal information, especially when used to make decisions.
items.question_text: A credit scoring bureau refuses to correct an erroneous loan default status on a debtor's record for two years. Which principle is violated?
options: Transparency
Accuracy
Proportionality
Decentralization
items.correct_answer: Accuracy
items.explanation: Failing to maintain correct and up-to-date personal data directly violates the principle of Accuracy.

items.lesson_concept: Accountability mandates that PICs implement measures (policies, organizational controls, audits) and be able to demonstrate compliance with the DPA.
items.question_text: A company has good internal cybersecurity but maintains zero written privacy manuals, data governance logs, or staff training records. Which principle is compromised?
options: Accountability
Confidentiality
Proportionality
Fairness
items.correct_answer: Accountability
items.explanation: Accountability requires demonstrating compliance through documented organizational policies, technical safeguards, and audit trails.

items.lesson_concept: Consent under the DPA must be freely given, specific, informed, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.question_text: Which of the following is an essential statutory requirement for valid consent under the DPA?
options: It can be assumed through pre-ticked checkboxes.
It must be freely given, specific, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
It must be notarized before a public attorney.
It must be renewed every 30 days.
items.correct_answer: It must be freely given, specific, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.explanation: Section 3(b) requires consent to be freely given, specific, informed, and properly evidenced.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 12, lawful criteria for processing PI include consent, contract fulfillment, legal obligation, vital interests, public authority, and legitimate interests.
items.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a lawful basis for processing standard Personal Information under Section 12?
options: Fulfillment of a contract
Compliance with a legal obligation
Commercial profitability of the PIC without balancing rights
Protection of vital interests of the data subject
items.correct_answer: Commercial profitability of the PIC without balancing rights
items.explanation: Commercial profit alone is not a lawful basis unless justified under a legitimate interest balancing test.

items.lesson_concept: Processing is lawful without separate consent when necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is a party.
items.question_text: An airline collects passenger full names and passport details to issue booked international flight tickets. What is the primary lawful basis?
options: National Emergency
Fulfillment of a Contract
Public Authority
Voluntary Donation
items.correct_answer: Fulfillment of a Contract
items.explanation: Processing passenger information is necessary to fulfill the ticket purchase and carriage contract.

items.lesson_concept: Processing SPI is strictly prohibited except for statutory grounds under Section 13: consent, existing law, life/health protection, public organizations, medical treatment, or legal claims.
items.question_text: Which of the following is a recognized lawful ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13?
options: General Legitimate Interest
Protection of Life and Health when subject is physically unable to express consent
Unilateral corporate policy
Direct targeted behavioral advertising
items.correct_answer: Protection of Life and Health when subject is physically unable to express consent
items.explanation: Section 13(c) permits processing SPI to protect life and health when consent cannot be legally or physically given.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate interest applies strictly to general Personal Information (Section 12) and cannot justify processing Sensitive Personal Information (Section 13).
items.question_text: An employer claims 'Legitimate Interest' to conduct genetic screenings on job applicants. Is this legally permissible?
options: Yes, if documented in internal HR manuals.
Yes, provided applicants do not verbally object.
No, Legitimate Interest is not a valid legal ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13.
No, unless approved by the Department of Labor.
items.correct_answer: No, Legitimate Interest is not a valid legal ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13.
items.explanation: Genetic data is SPI under Section 3(l), and Legitimate Interest cannot serve as a lawful basis under Section 13.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 13(f), processing SPI is permissible without consent when necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.
items.question_text: A law firm collects a defendant's past criminal history (SPI) to prepare a court defense in ongoing litigation. What is the lawful ground?
options: Consent of the opposing party
Establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims
Public Organization Exception
National Emergency
items.correct_answer: Establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims
items.explanation: Section 13(f) explicitly permits SPI processing for legal claims and court proceedings.

items.lesson_concept: The NPC Legitimate Interest Test requires three elements: Purpose Test (legitimate objective), Necessity Test (processing is necessary), and Balancing Test (does not override data subject rights).
items.question_text: What three tests must a PIC satisfy to lawfully rely on Legitimate Interest under NPC guidance?
options: Legality, Profitability, and Scalability tests
Purpose Test, Necessity Test, and Balancing Test
Consent Test, Identity Test, and Disclosure Test
Security Test, Integrity Test, and Redundancy Test
items.correct_answer: Purpose Test, Necessity Test, and Balancing Test
items.explanation: The Legitimate Interest Assessment requires satisfying the Purpose, Necessity, and Balancing tests.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to be Informed guarantees that a data subject must be told whether personal data pertaining to them is being processed.
items.question_text: Which right ensures that individuals are notified before their personal data enters an automated processing system?
options: Right to Rectify
Right to be Informed
Right to Data Portability
Right to Erasure
items.correct_answer: Right to be Informed
items.explanation: The Right to be Informed mandates notification prior to data entry into a processing system.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Access allows data subjects to demand reasonable access to contents of their personal data, sources, recipients, and reasons for disclosure.
items.question_text: What right gives a data subject the authority to request a copy of the specific personal data held by a company?
options: Right to Object
Right to Access
Right to Damages
Right to Portability
items.correct_answer: Right to Access
items.explanation: The Right to Access allows individuals to inspect and obtain copies of their personal data held by a PIC.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Object gives subjects the power to withhold or withdraw consent for processing, especially for direct marketing, profiling, or automated processing.
items.question_text: When a customer objects to data processing for direct marketing, what must the PIC do?
options: Charge a processing cancellation fee.
Continue processing for 30 business days.
Immediately stop processing for direct marketing.
Forward the data to another processor.
items.correct_answer: Immediately stop processing for direct marketing.
items.explanation: Upon an objection to direct marketing, the PIC must immediately cease processing without exception.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Rectify allows a data subject to dispute inaccuracies or errors in personal data and have the PIC correct them immediately.
items.question_text: If a subscriber identifies a misspelled surname and incorrect address in a billing portal, which right allows them to demand immediate correction?
options: Right to Portability
Right to Rectify
Right to Damages
Right to Erasure
items.correct_answer: Right to Rectify
items.explanation: The Right to Rectify gives individuals the right to have inaccurate or outdated data corrected.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure or Blocking allows individuals to demand removal or destruction of personal data that is incomplete, outdated, false, or unlawfully obtained.
items.question_text: Under which circumstance can a data subject rightfully demand the erasure or blocking of their data?
options: When data is being used for unauthorized purposes.
When the data is needed to comply with an active court order.
When the PIC is conducting an ongoing tax audit.
When the data subject simply regrets making an authorized purchase.
items.correct_answer: When data is being used for unauthorized purposes.
items.explanation: Erasure or blocking applies when data is outdated, false, unlawfully obtained, or used for unauthorized purposes.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure is not absolute and cannot be exercised when retention is required by statutory laws, court orders, or ongoing legal obligations.
items.question_text: A bank customer closes their account and demands immediate deletion of all past financial transaction records. The bank refuses, citing a 5-year AMLA record-retention rule. Is the bank justified?
options: No, the Right to Erasure is absolute upon account closure.
Yes, statutory legal obligations to retain records override the right to erasure.
No, unless the NPC grants an explicit waiver.
Yes, but only if the customer agrees in writing.
items.correct_answer: Yes, statutory legal obligations to retain records override the right to erasure.
items.explanation: Legal retention requirements (such as AMLA or tax laws) supersede the right to erasure.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Data Portability allows data subjects to obtain their electronic data in an interoperable, structured, commonly used format.
items.question_text: Which format standard best fulfills a user's Right to Data Portability request when moving data between cloud platforms?
options: An unsearchable printed physical paper document.
A structured, commonly used, machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV).
A proprietary encrypted binary file readable only by the issuing vendor.
A scanned low-resolution JPEG of a monitor screen.
items.correct_answer: A structured, commonly used, machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV).
items.explanation: Data portability requires providing data in an electronic, structured, and commonly used machine-readable format.

items.lesson_concept: Section 17 states that lawful heirs and assigns of a data subject may invoke the data subject's rights after death or incapacity.
items.question_text: Following the sudden passing of an account holder, can their legal heirs invoke the Right to Access and Data Portability on the deceased's accounts?
options: No, privacy rights expire immediately upon death.
Yes, lawful heirs and assigns may invoke data subject rights after death or incapacity.
No, unless authorized by a presidential decree.
Yes, but strictly limited to the Right to Erasure.
items.correct_answer: Yes, lawful heirs and assigns may invoke data subject rights after death or incapacity.
items.explanation: Section 17 explicitly establishes the transmissibility of data subject rights to lawful heirs and assigns.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA prescribes criminal penalties including mandatory imprisonment and fines for violations such as unauthorized processing and negligent access.
items.question_text: What type of penalties can regular courts impose for serious offenses defined under the Data Privacy Act?
options: Only public apologies
Imprisonment and criminal fines
Community service only
Administrative censure exclusively
items.correct_answer: Imprisonment and criminal fines
items.explanation: Offenses under Chapter VIII of the DPA carry penal sanctions of imprisonment and substantial fines.

items.lesson_concept: Unauthorized processing of personal information without consent or statutory authority carries imprisonment from 1 to 3 years and fines.
items.question_text: What offense is committed when a database admin extracts and sells customer data without authorization or lawful basis?
options: Data Portability Violation
Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information
Privileged Disclosure
Procedural Laches
items.correct_answer: Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information
items.explanation: Processing personal data without consent or legal authority constitutes the crime of Unauthorized Processing.

items.lesson_concept: Providing access to personal data due to negligence carries criminal imprisonment and fines, penalizing gross lack of basic security controls.
items.question_text: A sysadmin fails to set a password on an unencrypted public AWS S3 bucket holding employee SPI, exposing it online. Which DPA crime applies?
options: Malicious Disclosure
Accessing Personal Information Due to Negligence
Identity Theft under Cybercrime Act only
Breach of Warranty
items.correct_answer: Accessing Personal Information Due to Negligence
items.explanation: Section 26 penalizes accessing or providing access to personal or sensitive personal information due to negligence.

items.lesson_concept: Section 30 penalizes the intentional concealment of security breaches involving personal data after having knowledge of its occurrence.
items.question_text: A security manager discovers a massive breach of sensitive financial data but deletes the incident logs to hide it from the NPC. What crime was committed?
options: Improper Disposal
Concealment of Security Breaches
Unlawful Interception
Digital Contempt
items.correct_answer: Concealment of Security Breaches
items.explanation: Section 30 explicitly penalizes the intentional concealment of a qualifying security breach.

items.lesson_concept: Section 34 states that if the offender is a corporation, the penalty shall be imposed on responsible officers who participated in or allowed the crime through gross negligence.
items.question_text: A fintech firm is found guilty of unauthorized processing because its board ordered the bypass of privacy controls. Who incurs criminal liability?
options: Only the junior developer who wrote the code.
The responsible corporate officers who participated in or permitted the commission through gross negligence.
The corporation's external legal counsel.
No individual, since the firm is a distinct juridical entity.
items.correct_answer: The responsible corporate officers who participated in or permitted the commission through gross negligence.
items.explanation: Section 34 pierces corporate liability to penalize responsible officers who directed or allowed the offense.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 2022-01 authorizes administrative fines of up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income for grave infractions of the DPA and NPC issuances.
items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 2022-01, what is the maximum administrative fine the NPC can impose for grave infractions based on annual gross income?
options: Up to 1% of annual gross income
Up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income
A flat rate of PHP 10,000
Up to 50% of total company assets
items.correct_answer: Up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income
items.explanation: NPC Circular 2022-01 sets administrative fines for grave infractions at up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 33, when a violation involves both SPI and regular PI or constitutes a combination of multiple offenses, higher penalty brackets apply.
items.question_text: An insider steals an unencrypted database containing health records, credit card info, and home addresses, then uploads it to a leak forum for profit. What is the consequence?
options: The offense receives minimum administrative warnings.
Severe compound penalties apply for combination of offenses involving SPI and malicious disclosure.
Charges are reduced to simple civil breach of contract.
The offender receives automatic immunity by paying restitution.
items.correct_answer: Severe compound penalties apply for combination of offenses involving SPI and malicious disclosure.
items.explanation: Section 33 mandates higher, compounded criminal penalties when multiple DPA offenses and SPI are involved.

items.lesson_concept: A security incident affects system CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability), whereas a personal data breach specifically compromises personal data.
items.question_text: What distinguishes a Personal Data Breach from a general Security Incident?
options: A data breach involves actual or reasonable belief of unauthorized compromise of personal data.
A security incident only involves hardware fires.
A data breach never involves software bugs.
They are 100% identical in all legal aspects.
items.correct_answer: A data breach involves actual or reasonable belief of unauthorized compromise of personal data.
items.explanation: A personal data breach is a specific security incident resulting in unlawful access, destruction, loss, or alteration of personal data.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 16-03 mandates notification to the NPC and affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowledge or reasonable belief of a qualifying breach.
items.question_text: Within what mandatory timeframe must a PIC notify the NPC upon reasonable belief of a qualifying personal data breach?
options: 24 hours
48 hours
72 hours
7 working days
items.correct_answer: 72 hours
items.explanation: Section 20(f) of the DPA and NPC Circular 16-03 establish a strict 72-hour notification timeline.

items.lesson_concept: Mandatory breach notification requires ALL three: 1) involves SPI/financial info, 2) unauthorized acquisition occurred, 3) poses real risk of serious harm.
items.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three mandatory criteria triggering the 72-hour notification under NPC Circular 16-03?
options: Sensitive Personal Information or identity fraud data is involved.
Data was acquired by an unauthorized person.
The company's stock price dropped by at least 10%.
The breach poses a real risk of serious harm to data subjects.
items.correct_answer: The company's stock price dropped by at least 10%.
items.explanation: Stock performance is irrelevant; notification is triggered by sensitive data, unauthorized acquisition, and real risk of serious harm.

items.lesson_concept: The Incident Response Life Cycle consists of Preparation, Detection and Analysis, Containment/Eradication/Recovery, and Post-Incident Activity.
items.question_text: In the Incident Response Life Cycle, in which phase does an organization isolate affected network segments to stop ongoing data exfiltration?
options: Preparation
Containment, Eradication, and Recovery
Post-Incident Analysis
DPO Appointment
items.correct_answer: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery
items.explanation: Isolating compromised systems to stop data leaks occurs during the Containment, Eradication, and Recovery phase.

items.lesson_concept: A temporary system outage (availability breach) without unauthorized acquisition or real risk of serious harm does not trigger mandatory 72-hour NPC notification.
items.question_text: A power surge shuts down a university server for 3 hours. Internal logs confirm no data was altered or accessed by unauthorized third parties. Is a 72-hour NPC notification required?
options: Yes, all outages require 72-hour NPC notification.
No, because no data was acquired by an unauthorized party creating a risk of serious harm.
Yes, but only to the local police.
No, but all student IDs must be immediately re-issued.
items.correct_answer: No, because no data was acquired by an unauthorized party creating a risk of serious harm.
items.explanation: Without unauthorized acquisition or risk of serious harm, mandatory 72-hour reporting is not triggered, though it must be logged internally.

items.lesson_concept: If a stolen device contains encrypted data where the decryption key remains uncompromised, the risk of harm is mitigated, potentially exempting from data subject notice.
items.question_text: A company laptop containing biometric data is stolen, but full-disk AES-256 encryption is active and the key is secure. What is the notification obligation under NPC Circular 16-03?
options: Mandatory public TV broadcast within 24 hours.
The incident is logged; notification to data subjects may be exempted if encryption prevents unauthorized access.
Automatic fine of 5% gross income.
Immediate filing of criminal charges against the employee.
items.correct_answer: The incident is logged; notification to data subjects may be exempted if encryption prevents unauthorized access.
items.explanation: Under NPC Circular 16-03, strong encryption that renders data unreadable to unauthorized parties can exempt the PIC from notifying data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: All security incidents—whether qualifying for mandatory 72-hour notice or not—must be documented in an internal incident log and summarized in an Annual Security Incident Report to the NPC.
items.question_text: Must a PIC document minor security incidents (e.g., thwarted phishing emails, minor temporary glitches) that did not require a 72-hour breach notice?
options: No, minor incidents can be discarded immediately.
Yes, all security incidents must be documented internally and submitted annually in the Annual Security Incident Report.
Only if requested by a court order.
No, only criminal convictions require documentation.
items.correct_answer: Yes, all security incidents must be documented internally and submitted annually in the Annual Security Incident Report.
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-03 requires maintaining internal records of all incidents and submitting an Annual Security Incident Report to the NPC.

items.lesson_concept: When a PIP experiences a data breach, it must notify the PIC immediately without unreasonable delay to enable the PIC to meet its 72-hour NPC reporting window.
items.question_text: A third-party cloud hosting provider (PIP) discovers a breach of patient data belonging to a hospital client (PIC). What is the PIP's legal duty regarding notification?
options: The PIP can wait 30 days before emailing the hospital.
The PIP must notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without unreasonable delay.
The PIP bypasses the hospital and files an exclusive report without informing the hospital.
The PIP is immune from reporting obligations.
items.correct_answer: The PIP must notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without unreasonable delay.
items.explanation: A PIP must notify the PIC without unreasonable delay so the PIC can fulfill its 72-hour statutory notification obligations to the NPC and affected data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: Processing refers to any operation performed upon personal data including collection, recording, organization, storage, updating, modification, retrieval, consultation, use, consolidation, blocking, erasure, or destruction.
items.question_text: Under the DPA, which of the following activities is strictly considered as 'Processing' of personal data?
options: Only the permanent deletion of data.
Only the collection and storage of data.
Any operation performed upon personal data, including collection, storage, modification, and destruction.
Only the selling of data to third parties.
items.correct_answer: Any operation performed upon personal data, including collection, storage, modification, and destruction.
items.explanation: Processing is a comprehensive term under Section 3(j) that covers virtually any operation performed on personal data from collection to destruction.

items.lesson_concept: Transparency requires that data subjects be informed of the nature, purpose, and extent of the processing using clear and plain language.
items.question_text: A mobile application uses a 50-page Terms of Service agreement written entirely in dense legal Latin to explain its data collection practices. Which privacy principle is most directly violated?
options: Legitimate Purpose
Transparency
Proportionality
Data Minimization
items.correct_answer: Transparency
items.explanation: Transparency requires that information regarding data processing be easily accessible and understandable, utilizing clear and plain language.

items.lesson_concept: Processing standard Personal Information is lawful when it is necessary to protect vitally important interests of the data subject, including life and health.
items.question_text: During a massive flood, a local government unit (LGU) shares the home addresses (PI) of stranded residents with private rescue organizations without the residents' prior consent. Is this lawful?
options: No, because the LGU did not conduct a Privacy Impact Assessment.
No, because consent is strictly required for any sharing of home addresses.
Yes, because the processing is necessary to protect the vitally important interests of the data subjects.
Yes, but only if the residents sign a waiver after being rescued.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because the processing is necessary to protect the vitally important interests of the data subjects.
items.explanation: Section 12(d) allows processing without consent when necessary to protect vitally important interests of the data subject, such as in life-threatening emergencies.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Damages allows data subjects to be indemnified for any damages sustained due to inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, false, unlawfully obtained, or unauthorized use of personal data.
items.question_text: Which right empowers a data subject to seek financial compensation if they suffer harm due to a company's negligent handling of their personal data?
options: Right to Rectify
Right to Damages
Right to Object
Right to File a Complaint
items.correct_answer: Right to Damages
items.explanation: The Right to Damages specifically provides for indemnification for harm caused by DPA violations.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA applies to processing done outside the Philippines if it relates to personal information about a Philippine citizen or resident.
items.question_text: An Australian university with no offices in the Philippines accepts an enrollment application from a Filipino citizen living in Cebu. The university's database in Sydney is later hacked, exposing the student's data. Does the Philippine NPC have jurisdiction to investigate the university?
options: No, because the university has no physical equipment or branch in the Philippines.
No, the jurisdiction is strictly limited to Australian regulatory bodies.
Yes, because the processing relates to the personal information of a Philippine citizen.
Yes, but only if the student files a lawsuit in an Australian court first.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because the processing relates to the personal information of a Philippine citizen.
items.explanation: Section 6 of the DPA applies extraterritorially to foreign entities processing the data of Philippine citizens or residents, granting the NPC jurisdiction.

items.lesson_concept: Disclosing personal data with malice or bad faith constitutes the crime of Malicious Disclosure, which carries heavier penalties than negligence.
items.question_text: An angry employee steals a colleague's performance review (SPI) and posts it on a public forum to intentionally humiliate them. What specific DPA offense is this?
options: Accessing due to Negligence
Concealment of Security Breaches
Malicious Disclosure
Unauthorized Processing
items.correct_answer: Malicious Disclosure
items.explanation: Publishing the data to intentionally humiliate someone demonstrates malice and bad faith, fitting the crime of Malicious Disclosure (Section 27).

items.lesson_concept: A PIC may be exempted from notifying data subjects of a breach if the NPC determines that such notification would hinder a criminal investigation.
items.question_text: A bank suffers a data breach and the NBI requests the bank to temporarily withhold notifying the affected customers to avoid tipping off the hackers during a sting operation. What is the proper legal procedure?
options: The bank can unilaterally decide to withhold notification.
The bank must still notify the customers within 72 hours, as the DPA supersedes the NBI.
The bank must formally request the NPC for an exemption or postponement of notification to data subjects.
The bank must publish a blind notice in a national newspaper instead.
items.correct_answer: The bank must formally request the NPC for an exemption or postponement of notification to data subjects.
items.explanation: Only the NPC has the authority to officially postpone or exempt a PIC from notifying data subjects to protect a law enforcement investigation.

items.lesson_concept: A Data Subject is an individual whose personal, sensitive personal, or privileged information is processed.
items.question_text: In the context of the Data Privacy Act, who is considered the 'Data Subject'?
options: The IT administrator managing the database.
The individual whose personal information is being processed.
The company collecting the data.
The Data Protection Officer (DPO).
items.correct_answer: The individual whose personal information is being processed.
items.explanation: The Data Subject is the specific natural person to whom the personal data belongs.

items.lesson_concept: Consent must be freely given. If providing consent is made a mandatory prerequisite for a service where the data is not actually necessary, the consent is legally invalid.
items.question_text: A flashlight app requires users to consent to sharing their GPS location before the app will turn on the phone's LED light. Is this consent valid under the DPA?
options: Yes, because the user explicitly clicked 'Agree'.
Yes, because it is a free application.
No, because the consent is not 'freely given' if the service is made conditional on data processing that is unnecessary for the service.
No, because GPS data is classified as Privileged Information.
items.correct_answer: No, because the consent is not 'freely given' if the service is made conditional on data processing that is unnecessary for the service.
items.explanation: Consent is invalid if it is forced. Requiring irrelevant data (GPS) as a condition to use a basic service (flashlight) violates both Consent and Proportionality rules.

items.lesson_concept: If a data subject's rights are violated and the PIC fails to address the issue, the subject has the right to file a formal complaint with the National Privacy Commission.
items.question_text: A data subject repeatedly asks a company to rectify an error in their billing profile, but the company ignores the requests for 60 days. What is the data subject's most appropriate next step under the DPA?
options: File a complaint with the National Privacy Commission (NPC).
Hack the company's servers to change the data.
File a criminal case directly with the Supreme Court.
Do nothing, as companies have up to 1 year to rectify data.
items.correct_answer: File a complaint with the National Privacy Commission (NPC).
items.explanation: The Right to File a Complaint allows individuals to escalate unresolved grievances directly to the NPC for investigation and adjudication.

items.lesson_concept: The NPC issues Circulars to enforce the DPA. However, administrative circulars cannot override or expand the statutory laws passed by Congress.
items.question_text: If a new NPC Circular contradicts a specific provision explicitly written in the Data Privacy Act of 2012, which legal rule takes precedence?
options: The NPC Circular, because it is the most recent.
The Data Privacy Act of 2012, because statutes override administrative issuances.
Neither; the matter is suspended until the President decides.
The NPC Circular, because the NPC has supreme quasi-judicial power.
items.correct_answer: The Data Privacy Act of 2012, because statutes override administrative issuances.
items.explanation: In the Philippine legal hierarchy, an administrative issuance (like an NPC Circular) must conform to the statute (RA 10173) it aims to implement.

items.lesson_concept: Processing personal data strictly for journalistic, artistic, or literary purposes is exempt from the DPA to protect freedom of the press.
items.question_text: A news agency publishes the private travel logs of a public official to expose tax fraud. The official files a DPA complaint. Is the news agency liable for unauthorized processing?
options: Yes, travel logs are strictly confidential.
No, because processing for journalistic purposes is a statutory exemption under the DPA.
Yes, they must secure the official's written consent first.
No, but they must pay an administrative fine.
items.correct_answer: No, because processing for journalistic purposes is a statutory exemption under the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 4(d) exempts personal information processed for journalistic purposes to uphold press freedom and public interest.

items.lesson_concept: Information relating to individuals performing services under contract for a government institution is excluded from the DPA.
items.question_text: A private software developer is contracted to build an inventory system for a local government unit. A citizen requests the developer's name and contract details. Are these details protected by the DPA?
options: Yes, all private contractor data is protected.
No, information relating to individuals performing services under a government contract is excluded from the DPA.
Yes, unless the developer explicitly waives their rights.
No, but only if the contract is worth more than 1 million pesos.
items.correct_answer: No, information relating to individuals performing services under a government contract is excluded from the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 4(b) excludes information relating to individuals performing services under contract for a government institution to promote transparency.

items.lesson_concept: Privileged Information refers to data protected under the Rules of Court, such as communications between a doctor and patient, or lawyer and client.
items.question_text: Which of the following constitutes 'Privileged Information' under the DPA?
options: A student's grades.
An employee's salary.
Confidential communications between a patient and their psychiatrist.
A customer's credit card number.
items.correct_answer: Confidential communications between a patient and their psychiatrist.
items.explanation: Doctor-patient communications are legally privileged under the Rules of Court, classifying them as Privileged Information.

items.lesson_concept: A PIC decides the 'why' and 'how' of processing. A PIP only acts on the documented instructions of the PIC.
items.question_text: A developer builds an offline Point-of-Sale (POS) software and licenses it to a retail store. The store uses the software locally to process customer transactions. The developer has no access to the store's local database. Who is the Personal Information Controller (PIC)?
options: The software developer.
The retail store.
Both the developer and the store (Joint Controllers).
The customers.
items.correct_answer: The retail store.
items.explanation: The retail store determines the purpose and means of collecting the customer data. The developer merely provided the tool and has no access, so the store is the PIC.

items.lesson_concept: Biometric data used to uniquely identify an individual (e.g., fingerprints, facial recognition) is classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: A maritime company requires deckhands to log their attendance using a TTL serial fingerprint reader. Under the DPA, what classification is this fingerprint data?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information
Privileged Information
Public Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information
items.explanation: Biometrics used to uniquely identify an individual are classified as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI).

items.lesson_concept: Proportionality requires that the data collected must be adequate, relevant, and not excessive in relation to the declared purpose.
items.question_text: A website offering free video editing tutorials requires users to submit their passport copy before they can watch the videos. This violates the principle of:
options: Transparency
Legitimate Purpose
Proportionality
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Proportionality
items.explanation: Asking for a passport to watch free tutorials is highly excessive and unnecessary for the purpose, violating Proportionality.

items.lesson_concept: Personal data must be processed fairly and lawfully, and not used for a secondary purpose incompatible with the original declared purpose.
items.question_text: A solar panel installation company collects customer phone numbers for warranty support. Two years later, they sell the list to a telemarketing firm selling insurance. Which principle was violated?
options: Accountability
Accuracy
Legitimate Purpose
Proportionality
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: Selling the data to third-party telemarketers is completely incompatible with the original declared purpose (warranty support).

items.lesson_concept: The principle of Accountability mandates that organizations implement verifiable measures to demonstrate compliance, starting with appointing a DPO.
items.question_text: Which principle places the burden on the Personal Information Controller to demonstrate compliance by implementing active security measures and designating a Data Protection Officer?
options: Transparency
Fairness
Proportionality
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Accountability
items.explanation: Accountability requires the PIC to take ownership of the data and prove they have organizational, physical, and technical measures in place.

items.lesson_concept: Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.question_text: According to the DPA, what is an essential characteristic of valid 'Consent'?
options: It can be assumed if the user does not object.
It must be evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
It must be renewed annually.
It is only required for minors.
items.correct_answer: It must be evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.explanation: Section 3(b) mandates that valid consent must be clearly evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.

items.lesson_concept: Processing is lawful if it is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is a party.
items.question_text: An IT company requires its new remote developers to provide their bank account numbers to disburse their monthly salaries. What is the lawful basis for collecting this data?
options: Legitimate Interest
Compliance with a Legal Obligation
Fulfillment of a Contract
Vital Interests
items.correct_answer: Fulfillment of a Contract
items.explanation: Paying the employee is a fundamental necessity for fulfilling the employment contract.

items.lesson_concept: SPI can be processed without consent if necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.
items.question_text: A law firm collects the past criminal records (SPI) of their client to prepare a defense in an ongoing court trial. Is this lawful without explicit consent?
options: No, criminal records can never be processed.
Yes, under the exception for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.
No, unless the NPC issues a special permit.
Yes, but only if the data is pseudonymized.
items.correct_answer: Yes, under the exception for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.
items.explanation: Section 13(f) explicitly allows the processing of SPI when necessary for court proceedings or legal claims.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate interest is a valid basis for standard PI (Section 12), but it is never a valid lawful basis for Sensitive Personal Information (Section 13).
items.question_text: A company wants to collect the religious affiliations of its employees to analyze workplace diversity, claiming 'Legitimate Interest'. Is this legally valid?
options: Yes, workplace diversity is a valid legitimate interest.
No, because religious affiliation is SPI, and legitimate interest cannot be used as a lawful basis for processing SPI.
Yes, provided they notify the employees first.
No, unless they share the data with the government.
items.correct_answer: No, because religious affiliation is SPI, and legitimate interest cannot be used as a lawful basis for processing SPI.
items.explanation: Religious affiliation is Sensitive Personal Information (SPI). Section 13 does not list Legitimate Interest as a valid exception for processing SPI.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Access allows subjects to demand information on what data is held, how it is processed, and who it has been disclosed to.
items.question_text: Which right allows a user to demand a list of all third-party vendors that a company has shared their personal data with?
options: Right to Data Portability
Right to Access
Right to Rectify
Right to Object
items.correct_answer: Right to Access
items.explanation: The Right to Access includes the right to know the names and addresses of recipients to whom the personal data has been disclosed.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Rectify allows subjects to dispute inaccuracies. The PIC must correct it immediately unless the request is vexatious or unreasonable.
items.question_text: A data subject notices their birthdate is incorrectly listed on their health insurance portal and requests a correction. What is the PIC's obligation?
options: Correct it during the next annual audit.
Correct the inaccuracy immediately and accordingly, unless the request is vexatious.
Require the data subject to file a lawsuit first.
Delete the account entirely.
items.correct_answer: Correct the inaccuracy immediately and accordingly, unless the request is vexatious.
items.explanation: Section 16(d) dictates that inaccuracies must be rectified immediately upon the data subject's request.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure is not absolute. It can be denied if the data is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation.
items.question_text: A user demands an online payment platform erase their 3-year transaction history. The platform refuses, citing a central bank regulation requiring 5-year data retention for anti-money laundering. Is the platform justified?
options: No, the Right to Erasure overrides central bank regulations.
Yes, because the data is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the PIC is subject.
No, unless the NPC grants a specific exemption.
Yes, but only if the user owes the platform money.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because the data is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the PIC is subject.
items.explanation: Statutory retention laws (like AMLA) take precedence over a user's request for erasure.

items.lesson_concept: Data portability requires the PIC to provide the data in an electronic, structured, and commonly used format to prevent vendor lock-in.
items.question_text: To properly fulfill a 'Right to Data Portability' request, how must the PIC provide the data?
options: Printed on physical paper.
In a proprietary format that can only be read by the PIC's software.
In an electronic, structured, and commonly used format.
As a verbal summary over the phone.
items.correct_answer: In an electronic, structured, and commonly used format.
items.explanation: The core purpose of portability is interoperability, requiring structured electronic formats like JSON or CSV.

items.lesson_concept: Data subject rights are transmissible. Lawful heirs and assigns may invoke the rights of the data subject after their death or incapacity.
items.question_text: After a patient passes away due to medical malpractice, can their legal heirs invoke the Right to Access to obtain the deceased patient's medical records?
options: No, privacy rights expire upon death.
Yes, the lawful heirs can invoke the rights of the data subject under the principle of transmissibility.
No, only a court judge can access deceased records.
Yes, but only if the patient signed a DPA waiver before dying.
items.correct_answer: Yes, the lawful heirs can invoke the rights of the data subject under the principle of transmissibility.
items.explanation: Section 17 of the DPA explicitly allows lawful heirs to invoke the rights of a deceased or incapacitated data subject.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA imposes criminal penalties (imprisonment and fines) for offenses like unauthorized processing, malicious disclosure, and negligence.
items.question_text: Unlike some international privacy laws that only issue fines, what severe penalty can regular Philippine courts impose for violations of the DPA?
options: Loss of citizenship.
Mandatory imprisonment of the responsible officers.
Exile.
Community service.
items.correct_answer: Mandatory imprisonment of the responsible officers.
items.explanation: Chapter VIII of the DPA specifies mandatory imprisonment terms alongside fines for various privacy crimes.

items.lesson_concept: Accessing or providing access to personal data due to negligence—such as failing to set a password on a database—is a criminal offense.
items.question_text: An IT administrator accidentally leaves a cloud storage bucket containing employee tax IDs completely public, resulting in a data leak. What is the specific criminal offense?
options: Malicious Disclosure
Concealment of Security Breaches
Accessing Sensitive Personal Information Due to Negligence
Unauthorized Processing
items.correct_answer: Accessing Sensitive Personal Information Due to Negligence
items.explanation: Failing to secure the bucket is an act of gross negligence, triggering Section 26 of the DPA.

items.lesson_concept: When a corporation commits a DPA crime, the penalty is imposed on the responsible officers who participated in or allowed the crime through negligence.
items.question_text: A tech startup's CEO explicitly orders the engineering team to scrape and sell user data without consent. The NPC investigates. Who faces criminal imprisonment?
options: The startup as a juridical entity.
The NPC cannot imprison anyone in a startup.
The CEO and any other responsible officers who participated in the crime.
Only the DPO.
items.correct_answer: The CEO and any other responsible officers who participated in the crime.
items.explanation: Section 34 states that for juridical persons, the penalty is imposed on the responsible officers who ordered or allowed the violation.

items.lesson_concept: The NPC can impose administrative fines (up to 3-5% of gross income) for infractions like failing to appoint a DPO or failing to register processing systems.
items.question_text: If a Personal Information Controller repeatedly refuses to draft a Privacy Manual and register their processing systems, what action can the NPC directly take?
options: Issue an arrest warrant.
Impose administrative fines based on the company's annual gross income.
Shut down the company's physical office.
Confiscate the company's servers.
items.correct_answer: Impose administrative fines based on the company's annual gross income.
items.explanation: The NPC has quasi-judicial authority to levy administrative fines for regulatory infractions, as outlined in NPC Circular 2022-01.

items.lesson_concept: A security incident threatens system integrity/availability. A personal data breach specifically results in unauthorized access, loss, or alteration of personal data.
items.question_text: A company's website is defaced by hackers, but the underlying customer database remains fully secure and untouched. How is this event classified?
options: A mandatory personal data breach.
A security incident, but not a personal data breach.
A lawful exception.
A malicious disclosure.
items.correct_answer: A security incident, but not a personal data breach.
items.explanation: Because system integrity was affected (defacement), it is a security incident. Because no personal data was compromised, it is not a personal data breach.

items.lesson_concept: A PIC must notify the NPC within 72 hours upon knowledge of, or reasonable belief that, a qualifying personal data breach has occurred.
items.question_text: An organization confirms a massive breach of sensitive personal data on a Friday at 6:00 PM. When does the 72-hour deadline to notify the NPC expire?
options: Monday at 6:00 PM.
Wednesday at 6:00 PM (skipping weekends).
Friday at midnight.
Tuesday at 9:00 AM.
items.correct_answer: Monday at 6:00 PM.
items.explanation: The 72-hour rule runs continuously and includes weekends and holidays.

items.lesson_concept: Mandatory notification is triggered when the breach involves SPI or identity fraud data, is acquired by an unauthorized person, and risks serious harm.
items.question_text: Which of the following scenarios absolutely triggers the mandatory 72-hour breach notification to the NPC?
options: An encrypted laptop is stolen, but the encryption key is secure.
A server outage delays internal emails for 4 hours.
Hackers download an unencrypted database containing customer Social Security Numbers and passport copies.
An employee accidentally deletes a blank folder.
items.correct_answer: Hackers download an unencrypted database containing customer Social Security Numbers and passport copies.
items.explanation: This scenario meets all criteria: it involves SPI (passports/SSS), unauthorized acquisition (hackers), and creates a real risk of serious harm (identity theft).

items.lesson_concept: When a PIP suffers a breach, their legal duty is to notify the PIC immediately without undue delay, so the PIC can report to the NPC.
items.question_text: A cloud hosting vendor (PIP) realizes their servers were compromised, exposing the data of a hospital client (PIC). What must the vendor do?
options: Notify the NPC directly within 72 hours.
Notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without undue delay.
Notify the patients directly.
Wait for the hospital to discover it.
items.correct_answer: Notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without undue delay.
items.explanation: The PIP must inform the PIC immediately so the PIC can initiate their incident response and fulfill their statutory obligation to notify the NPC.

items.lesson_concept: Organizations are required to establish a Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) to prepare for, detect, and respond to breaches.
items.question_text: To comply with the 'Preparation' phase of the Incident Response Life Cycle under NPC Circular 16-03, what structural body must an organization create?
options: A Cybersecurity Board of Directors.
A Security Incident Response Team (SIRT).
An internal Police Force.
A Data Marketing Committee.
items.correct_answer: A Security Incident Response Team (SIRT).
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-03 explicitly mandates the creation of a data breach response team (SIRT).

items.lesson_concept: All security incidents must be logged internally, and a summary must be submitted to the NPC in an Annual Security Incident Report.
items.question_text: A company experiences several minor phishing attempts that are blocked by their firewall. No data is breached. Do they need to document these events?
options: No, blocked attempts are legally irrelevant.
Yes, they must be documented internally and summarized in the Annual Security Incident Report submitted to the NPC.
Only if the hackers demand a ransom.
Yes, but they must be reported within 72 hours.
items.correct_answer: Yes, they must be documented internally and summarized in the Annual Security Incident Report submitted to the NPC.
items.explanation: All security incidents, even minor ones that don't trigger mandatory notification, must be logged and included in the annual report.

items.lesson_concept: Intentionally failing to report a mandatory breach to the NPC to hide the incident constitutes Concealment of Security Breaches.
items.question_text: A Chief Information Officer discovers a massive leak of biometric data. Fearing bad PR, they order the IT team to wipe the logs and hide the event from the NPC. What specific crime is committed?
options: Unauthorized Processing
Concealment of Security Breaches
Malicious Disclosure
Data Portability Violation
items.correct_answer: Concealment of Security Breaches
items.explanation: Intentionally delaying or failing to notify the NPC of a qualifying breach to hide it is penalized under Section 30.

items.lesson_concept: The immediate priority upon discovering a breach is containment—stopping the active exfiltration of data.
items.question_text: During an active cyberattack where hackers are actively downloading a database, what is the most critical immediate step for the Security Incident Response Team?
options: Drafting the NPC notification letter.
Containment, such as disconnecting the affected servers from the network to stop the data theft.
Filing a civil lawsuit against the hackers.
Conducting a post-incident review.
items.correct_answer: Containment, such as disconnecting the affected servers from the network to stop the data theft.
items.explanation: Operational containment is the absolute first priority in incident response to prevent further data loss before administrative steps are taken.

items.lesson_concept: Under the principle of Proportionality, personal data shall not be retained longer than necessary for the fulfillment of the declared, specified, and legitimate purpose.
items.question_text: A tech company collects resumes from unsuccessful job applicants and keeps them in an active, unencrypted database indefinitely 'just in case' they need them in 10 years. Which DPA principle does this violate?
options: Transparency
Accuracy
Proportionality (specifically Data Retention limits)
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Proportionality (specifically Data Retention limits)
items.explanation: Retaining personal data indefinitely when it is no longer necessary for the immediate hiring purpose is excessive and violates the retention limits of the Proportionality principle.

items.lesson_concept: Privileged Information includes data protected under the Rules of Court, such as marital privilege, where a spouse cannot be forced to testify against the other regarding private communications.
items.question_text: A company investigator tries to force an employee to disclose private text messages sent by their spouse regarding a potential internal fraud case. What classification protects these text messages?
options: Sensitive Personal Information
General Personal Information
Public Domain Information
Privileged Information
items.correct_answer: Privileged Information
items.explanation: Spousal communications are protected under marital privilege in the Rules of Court, rendering them Privileged Information under the DPA.

items.lesson_concept: Processing personal data for purposes not authorized by the data subject or otherwise permitted by law constitutes the crime of Processing for Unauthorized Purposes.
items.question_text: A logistics company collects customer phone numbers specifically for package delivery updates. A rogue manager extracts this list and uses it to text political campaign ads. What offense has been committed?
options: Accessing Due to Negligence
Processing for Unauthorized Purposes
Concealment of Security Breaches
Data Portability Violation
items.correct_answer: Processing for Unauthorized Purposes
items.explanation: Using data collected for shipping to conduct political campaigning is a severe deviation from the authorized purpose, constituting a criminal offense under Section 28.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to be Informed requires that the data subject be notified of the processing details *before* their personal data enters the processing system.
items.question_text: A website collects user survey data but only displays its Privacy Notice on a 'Thank You' page *after* the user has submitted the form. Why is this a violation?
options: The Privacy Notice must be translated into multiple languages.
The Right to be Informed requires notification BEFORE the entry of personal data into the processing system.
The website must mail a physical copy of the notice.
Privacy Notices are not required for surveys.
items.correct_answer: The Right to be Informed requires notification BEFORE the entry of personal data into the processing system.
items.explanation: To ensure consent is informed, the data subject must understand the processing details prior to submitting their data, not after the fact.

items.lesson_concept: A system vulnerability or an unexploited open port is a security risk, but it does not constitute a personal data breach unless personal data is actually compromised.
items.question_text: During an annual audit, a penetration tester finds a critical flaw in a hospital's firewall that *could* allow access to patient records. However, logs prove no unauthorized access actually occurred. Is this a Personal Data Breach?
options: Yes, all critical vulnerabilities must be reported as data breaches within 72 hours.
Yes, because patient records are Sensitive Personal Information.
No, it is a vulnerability/security risk, but not a data breach since no personal data was unlawfully accessed or disclosed.
No, unless the media finds out about the vulnerability.
items.correct_answer: No, it is a vulnerability/security risk, but not a data breach since no personal data was unlawfully accessed or disclosed.
items.explanation: A data breach requires actual or reasonably suspected compromise of personal data. A discovered, unexploited vulnerability is an operational risk, not a breach.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA still applies to personal data even if it is publicly available. Scraping public data for automated profiling or facial recognition requires a lawful basis.
items.question_text: A tech startup creates a facial recognition database by scraping millions of publicly visible profile pictures from social media. Does the Data Privacy Act apply to this publicly available data?
options: No, data posted publicly loses all DPA protection.
Yes, the DPA applies to the processing of personal data regardless of whether it was sourced from the public domain.
No, as long as the startup does not sell the data.
Yes, but only if the individuals are government officials.
items.correct_answer: Yes, the DPA applies to the processing of personal data regardless of whether it was sourced from the public domain.
items.explanation: The NPC has repeatedly clarified that personal data does not lose its privacy protection merely because it is accessible in the public domain; a lawful basis is still required for processing.

items.lesson_concept: For minors or individuals without legal capacity, valid consent must be obtained from their parents or lawful legal guardians.
items.question_text: A mobile gaming app explicitly targeting 10-year-old children asks the players to click 'I Consent' to share their location data. Is this consent legally valid under the DPA?
options: Yes, electronic consent clicks are always valid.
No, because minors lack legal capacity; consent must be obtained from a parent or lawful guardian.
Yes, as long as the game is free to play.
No, unless the game has an educational purpose.
items.correct_answer: No, because minors lack legal capacity; consent must be obtained from a parent or lawful guardian.
items.explanation: Minors cannot legally grant valid consent. Processing their data based on consent requires authorization from a parent or legal guardian.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA distinguishes between negligent exposure (accidental) and malicious disclosure (intentional bad faith), with the latter carrying heavier penalties.
items.question_text: An IT administrator discovers their company is downsizing and, in retaliation, actively emails the entire corporate payroll database to a competing firm. What specific crime does this constitute?
options: Accessing Due to Negligence
Concealment of Security Breaches
Malicious Disclosure
Failure to Register
items.correct_answer: Malicious Disclosure
items.explanation: The deliberate and retaliatory act of leaking the database to a competitor demonstrates clear malice and bad faith, fitting the crime of Malicious Disclosure.

items.lesson_concept: The principle of Accuracy mandates that data must be accurate, complete, and kept up-to-date, especially if it affects the data subject's rights.
items.question_text: A user legally changes their name and provides the necessary court documents to a bank. The bank refuses to update their system because 'it takes too much administrative effort.' Which principle is the bank violating?
options: Proportionality
Transparency
Accuracy
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Accuracy
items.explanation: Refusing to update demonstrably incorrect or outdated personal data violates the principle of Accuracy.

items.lesson_concept: The final phase of the Incident Response Life Cycle is Post-Incident Activity, which involves reviewing what happened, learning from mistakes, and updating policies to prevent recurrence.
items.question_text: Following a successful containment and eradication of a malware infection, the Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) holds a meeting to rewrite their firewall policies based on the attack vectors used. Which phase of the Incident Response Life Cycle is this?
options: Preparation
Detection and Analysis
Containment, Eradication, and Recovery
Post-Incident Activity
items.correct_answer: Post-Incident Activity
items.explanation: Reviewing the incident, identifying lessons learned, and updating policies to prevent future breaches are the core components of the Post-Incident Activity phase.

items.lesson_concept: Republic Act No. 10173 is the primary law governing data privacy in the Philippines, officially known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
items.question_text: What does the acronym 'DPA' stand for in the context of Philippine privacy law?
options: Data Protection Authority
Data Privacy Act
Digital Privacy Agency
Data Processing Agreement
items.correct_answer: Data Privacy Act
items.explanation: DPA stands for the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173).

items.lesson_concept: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is the independent government agency mandated to administer and implement the Data Privacy Act.
items.question_text: Which government body is primarily responsible for enforcing the Data Privacy Act in the Philippines?
options: Department of Justice (DOJ)
National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)
National Privacy Commission (NPC)
Supreme Court
items.correct_answer: National Privacy Commission (NPC)
items.explanation: The NPC is the country's privacy watchdog and regulatory body created by the DPA.

items.lesson_concept: A Data Subject refers to an individual whose personal, sensitive personal, or privileged information is processed.
items.question_text: Under the Data Privacy Act, what term is used to describe the individual whose personal information is being collected or processed?
options: Data Owner
Data Subject
Data Controller
Data Client
items.correct_answer: Data Subject
items.explanation: The law formally refers to the individual whose data is processed as the 'Data Subject'.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information is any data from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained.
items.question_text: Which of the following is the most basic example of standard Personal Information?
options: A person's full name.
A person's genetic sequence.
A person's political affiliation.
A person's medical history.
items.correct_answer: A person's full name.
items.explanation: A full name is standard Personal Information. Genetics, politics, and health are considered Sensitive Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) requires stricter protection. It includes race, marital status, health, genetics, and government-issued IDs.
items.question_text: Which of these is explicitly categorized as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)?
options: A business email address.
An individual's health record.
A company phone number.
An office building address.
items.correct_answer: An individual's health record.
items.explanation: Information about an individual's health is strictly classified as Sensitive Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Controller (PIC) is a person or organization who controls the collection, holding, processing, or use of personal information.
items.question_text: What do you call the entity that determines the purpose and the means of processing personal data?
options: Data Subject
Personal Information Processor (PIP)
Personal Information Controller (PIC)
Data Protection Officer (DPO)
items.correct_answer: Personal Information Controller (PIC)
items.explanation: The PIC is the decision-maker that controls why and how data is processed.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Processor (PIP) is any natural or juridical person to whom a PIC outsources the processing of personal data.
items.question_text: If a company outsources data processing to a third party that only acts on given instructions, what is the third party called?
options: Personal Information Controller (PIC)
Personal Information Processor (PIP)
Data Protection Officer (DPO)
Privacy Commissioner
items.correct_answer: Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.explanation: An entity that processes data strictly on behalf of and according to the instructions of a PIC is a PIP.

items.lesson_concept: Every PIC and PIP must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) who is accountable for ensuring the organization complies with the DPA.
items.question_text: What is the primary role of a Data Protection Officer (DPO)?
options: To fix broken servers.
To ensure the organization complies with the Data Privacy Act.
To handle all company public relations.
To sell data to advertisers.
items.correct_answer: To ensure the organization complies with the Data Privacy Act.
items.explanation: The DPO is the individual designated to oversee and ensure the organization's compliance with privacy laws.

items.lesson_concept: Transparency requires organizations to inform data subjects about how their data will be processed using clear and plain language.
items.question_text: Which privacy principle dictates that you must clearly inform data subjects about what data you collect and why?
options: Transparency
Proportionality
Confidentiality
Legitimate Purpose
items.correct_answer: Transparency
items.explanation: Transparency ensures nothing is done in secret and the individual understands the processing.

items.lesson_concept: Proportionality means processing must be adequate, relevant, suitable, necessary, and not excessive in relation to a declared purpose.
items.question_text: Which privacy principle dictates that an organization should only collect the absolute minimum amount of data necessary?
options: Accountability
Legitimate Purpose
Proportionality
Accuracy
items.correct_answer: Proportionality
items.explanation: Proportionality strictly discourages excessive data collection.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate Purpose means data must only be processed for specific, declared, and lawful reasons.
items.question_text: If a company collects data for a contest, but later uses it to send spam marketing emails without permission, which principle is violated?
options: Data Portability
Legitimate Purpose
Proportionality
Accountability
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: Using data for a secondary, incompatible purpose violates the principle of Legitimate Purpose.

items.lesson_concept: Consent is any freely given, specific, informed indication of will whereby the data subject agrees to the processing of their data.
items.question_text: Under the DPA, what must consent be in order to be considered valid?
options: Assumed based on silence.
Freely given, specific, and informed.
Forced as a condition of service.
Given verbally without any recording.
items.correct_answer: Freely given, specific, and informed.
items.explanation: Consent must be explicitly and freely given, and the data subject must know exactly what they are agreeing to.

items.lesson_concept: While consent is a common lawful basis, it is not the only one. Data can also be processed to fulfill a contract, comply with a law, or protect a life.
items.question_text: Is 'Consent' the only legal way an organization can process Personal Information?
options: Yes, consent is always required.
No, there are other lawful bases such as fulfilling a contract or complying with a legal obligation.
Yes, unless the person is a government employee.
No, but only if the data is printed on paper.
items.correct_answer: No, there are other lawful bases such as fulfilling a contract or complying with a legal obligation.
items.explanation: The DPA provides several lawful criteria for processing data beyond just consent (e.g., contracts, legal obligations, legitimate interests).

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Access gives data subjects the right to obtain a copy of their personal data held by an organization.
items.question_text: Which right allows you to ask a company for a copy of all the personal data they currently hold about you?
options: Right to Object
Right to Access
Right to Rectify
Right to Erasure
items.correct_answer: Right to Access
items.explanation: The Right to Access empowers individuals to see exactly what information a company has on them.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Rectify is the right to dispute inaccuracies in personal data and have the PIC correct them.
items.question_text: If a bank spells your name wrong on your account profile, which right allows you to demand they fix it?
options: Right to Erasure
Right to Object
Right to Rectify
Right to Data Portability
items.correct_answer: Right to Rectify
items.explanation: The Right to Rectify allows data subjects to correct inaccurate or outdated information.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure or Blocking allows a data subject to request the deletion of their data when it is no longer needed or was unlawfully processed.
items.question_text: Which right allows you to demand the deletion of your personal data from a company's database?
options: Right to Erasure or Blocking
Right to be Informed
Right to Rectify
Right to File a Complaint
items.correct_answer: Right to Erasure or Blocking
items.explanation: The Right to Erasure allows you to request the removal or destruction of your personal data.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA imposes severe penalties for violations, including heavy administrative fines and mandatory imprisonment for criminal offenses.
items.question_text: What type of penalties can be imposed on individuals who commit serious criminal violations of the Data Privacy Act?
options: Only a warning letter.
Only community service.
Imprisonment and monetary fines.
Suspension of internet access.
items.correct_answer: Imprisonment and monetary fines.
items.explanation: Criminal violations under the DPA carry mandatory imprisonment and fines.

items.lesson_concept: A security incident is an event that affects data protection or may compromise the availability, integrity, or confidentiality of a system.
items.question_text: What is the general term used for any event that compromises the availability, integrity, or confidentiality of an IT system?
options: A Security Incident
A Lawful Processing
A Consent Form
A Privacy Notice
items.correct_answer: A Security Incident
items.explanation: A security incident is the broad term for any threat or compromise to a system's security.

items.lesson_concept: A personal data breach is a specific type of security incident where personal data is actually compromised, lost, or unlawfully accessed.
items.question_text: What is the difference between a 'Security Incident' and a 'Personal Data Breach'?
options: There is no difference.
A personal data breach is a type of security incident that specifically involves the compromise of personal data.
A security incident only involves physical paper.
A data breach only happens to government agencies.
items.correct_answer: A personal data breach is a type of security incident that specifically involves the compromise of personal data.
items.explanation: All data breaches are security incidents, but a security incident is only a data breach if personal information is actually affected.

items.lesson_concept: Organizations must notify the NPC within 72 hours upon discovering a personal data breach that requires mandatory notification.
items.question_text: How many hours does an organization have to notify the National Privacy Commission (NPC) after discovering a mandatory reportable data breach?
options: 24 hours
48 hours
72 hours
96 hours
items.correct_answer: 72 hours
items.explanation: The NPC enforces a strict 72-hour notification rule for qualifying personal data breaches.

items.lesson_concept: The Data Privacy Act balances two interests: protecting the fundamental human right to privacy of communication while ensuring the free flow of information to promote innovation and growth.
items.question_text: According to the Declaration of Policy in Section 2 of the DPA, what are the two main interests the State seeks to balance?
options: Government surveillance and national security.
The right to privacy and the free flow of information to promote innovation and growth.
Corporate profitability and tax collection.
Freedom of the press and censorship.
items.correct_answer: The right to privacy and the free flow of information to promote innovation and growth.
items.explanation: The DPA recognizes that while privacy is a fundamental human right, the free flow of information is also necessary for innovation and economic growth.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA applies to the processing of all types of personal information and to any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing.
items.question_text: Does the Data Privacy Act apply only to large corporations?
options: Yes, it only applies to corporations with more than 250 employees.
No, it applies to any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing.
Yes, small businesses and individuals are automatically exempt.
No, it applies exclusively to government agencies.
items.correct_answer: No, it applies to any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing.
items.explanation: The law's scope is broad, covering both natural persons (individuals) and juridical persons (corporations, agencies) processing personal data.

items.lesson_concept: In Philippine jurisprudence, the right to privacy was recognized as an independent right in the landmark case of Morfe v. Mutuc, establishing it as a fundamental constitutional right.
items.question_text: Which landmark Philippine Supreme Court case explicitly recognized the right to privacy as an independent constitutional right?
options: Ople v. Torres
Disini v. Secretary of Justice
Morfe v. Mutuc
People v. Marti
items.correct_answer: Morfe v. Mutuc
items.explanation: In Morfe v. Mutuc (1968), the Supreme Court first explicitly recognized the right to privacy as a fundamental right rooted in the Constitution.

items.lesson_concept: Information regarding the official functions, position, or salary of government employees is excluded from the DPA to ensure public transparency.
items.question_text: A citizen requests the official salary grade of a municipal mayor. Can the mayor invoke the DPA to hide this information?
options: Yes, because a salary is Sensitive Personal Information.
No, because information about a government officer relating to their position or salary is explicitly excluded from the DPA.
Yes, unless the citizen pays an access fee.
No, but only if the mayor has been convicted of a crime.
items.correct_answer: No, because information about a government officer relating to their position or salary is explicitly excluded from the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 4(a) excludes data related to the official position, functions, and salary range of government employees from the DPA's coverage.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information is any data from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained.
items.question_text: Which of the following describes 'Personal Information' under the DPA?
options: Data that has been fully anonymized and cannot identify a person.
Any information from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably ascertained.
Only information that is kept secret by the government.
Data exclusively related to a person's medical history.
items.correct_answer: Any information from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably ascertained.
items.explanation: Section 3(g) defines Personal Information as any information that identifies or can reasonably identify an individual.

items.lesson_concept: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) includes data about race, marital status, health, genetics, and government-issued IDs.
items.question_text: Which of the following is an example of Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)?
options: A work email address.
A person's favorite color.
A person's blood type and medical diagnosis.
A public office phone number.
